explanation: Visit original nodes in inorder order and link consecutive nodes as previous/next through Left/Right. Save the original right child before changing links. The first node’s Left and final node’s Right are null.
timeComplexity: O(n) Every node is visited once and receives at most two list links.
spaceComplexity: O(h), where h is the original tree height The explicit stack or recursion follows at most the original tree height.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Inorder traversal visits original nodes in sorted order. Linking each visited node after its predecessor creates all required forward/backward links. Saving the original right child before rewiring preserves the unvisited traversal, and terminating the tail prevents a residual tree edge.
walkthrough: For tree [5,2,8,1,3], the visit order is 1,2,3,5,8. These same nodes become a list whose Left links point to their predecessors and Right links to their successors. The returned values are [1,2,3,5,8].
edgeCases: The head’s Left and tail’s Right must be null.
A one-node tree needs both list links cleared.
The traversal must not follow a newly written list link as a tree edge.
